per_probe.answer_text:
We taught the Two Ways to anyone coming toward the water - a way of life and a way of death, open before every person as a real choice. What that teaching asked of anyone, it asked of everyone. But you are asking us how we would have regarded you, and the honest answer is: we cannot say. What a particular household, in a particular city, would have made of any one person walking toward its door - that is not something our own record gives us. We can tell you what we taught. We can tell you what we asked of people. We cannot tell you how any one gathering would have received you.

If you are asking because you wonder whether people like you were there at all - enslaved members were among us, addressed in instruction, and two enslaved women were tortured for what they knew about us. But no enslaved voice survives. If you are asking because you are a woman - women were taught, greeted, and remembered among us, but no woman's own words survive in this window. If you are asking because you live outside a city - the record we left is urban; we cannot show you what a gathering in the countryside looked like.

It is not our place to judge what you are. We can only tell you honestly what we held, and name plainly where our own record falls silent.
